title: token usage, cost and context pressure reach the session row
asserts: a core that reads a CLI's transcript folds what each request spent onto SessionMeta.usage and broadcasts the row, so a client renders the token badge, the estimated spend and the context percentage without deriving anything itself. Cumulative counts only grow across requests; contextTokens is the newest request's input + cache, so it tracks what the window actually holds rather than what the session has spent in total. Without this every badge is blank, the sidebar spend total reads zero and a cost budget can never trip (juancode-8ti0).

steps.note: one billed request on a model the price table knows: 1000 input, 200 output, 3000 cache read, 500 cache write
same back-off as the transcript scenarios: the first bind attempt lands on the spawn banner, before the file exists
output is what marks a session worth re-reading, so this is what gets the written turn polled

the four counts are the CLI's own numbers; totalTokens is their sum; contextTokens is input + cache read + cache write, which is what the next request has to re-send, and deliberately excludes the 200 tokens of output. costUsd is an estimate from the model's published rates - 1000 at $3/MTok, cache read at 0.1x, cache write at 1.25x, 200 output at $15/MTok - asserted as a band because it is a float

a second request adds to the totals and REPLACES the context reading: spend is a tally, occupancy is a level. A core that summed contextTokens would report 9000 here and tell a user the window was 4.5% fuller than it is - and would never come back down when the CLI compacts
